title: Full Body-Maintain to Gain
author: Patrick B.
desc:
The program is built taking parts of Smolov's high frequency training philosophy for strength gains, a realistic view on people's often limited time, and personal feedback from over 10 years of lifting in hopes of reaching a wide range of lifters from the busy man to the dedicated gym goer.

Though ambitious, the "Maintain to Gain" program is the first attempt at combining the best of all training philosophies, mixing it with proven results and laying it out plainly for all to try.

There are no promises here but with careful consideration, 10+ years of lifting experience and multiple programs (some proving successful and others not) having been completed; I can assure you that there's no reason you can't hit 1 or more impressive PRs by the time you complete this program.

I hope everyone is willing to give this a shot even if at first glance it comes across as crazy or bullsh*t so we can grow and alter the program to be the best it can be.

Feel free to swap with French Press or Weighted Dips 
This should be a heavier/harder movement than later cable work and is only done once a week.
This is your last exercise so feel free to add a 4th set or make your 3rd a drop set ensuring you don't leave anything in the tank.
This is your secondary movement and should still be a bit harder than any machine work you will be doing. Choose a weight that you are comfortable with even on rep 10 but still struggle on last set
This is a bench variation movement so feel free to swap for CG/WG. The point of this exercise is to get more bench movement throughout the week so we constantly work on our muscles and pathway/form.
This is the final exercise of the day and you'll have a lot of rest before you hit quads again. Make sure you burn out. Try static hold  for 30 seconds on your last rep to really feel the fire.
Swap for standing calf raise if you wish. Its calves and not a big deal.
Use an EZ bar if you'd like as long as you keep the weight relatively heavy and move through a full range of motion it won't matter.
Use this time to do your favourite crunch variation and feel free to add in 3 sets of side bends or rotational movement if you have the energy and are feeling good.
Make sure you burn out here and feel free to use a bit of body English to get the final reps if need be.
Whether its rows or deads, try and add 10lbs/week to this movement and control the movement to prevent injury.
Whichever bench variation you didn't do earlier in the week, do now.

Either use this week as a 1RM test for your main movements or a deload before rerunning the program.
If you go for PR your 6th set should be at +2-5%  of your previous 1RM max
Aim for a 5-10lb increase to your PR

If you chose Deadlifts as your main back movement now is the time to test your 1RM.
If you chose to row you can also do a 1RM test OR see if your rep max has increased at previous 1RM.
